the phases of the three-dimensional $ N=2 $ supersymmetric gauge theory associated with the Weierstrauss model of an elliptically fibered fourfold with section are encoded in a box graph, which describes the representation graph of matter, and that the network of phases carries a structure that is reminiscent of a quasi-minuscule representation.

(1) the Coulomb branch phases of the low energy effective M-theory compactification on the singular Weierstrass fibration are in one-to-one correspondence with the set of all possible resolutions of this fibration, and (2) the set of all flop transitions between resolutions is encoded in a box graph that is a (quasi)-minuscule representation for a certain Lie algebra, which is the Lie algebra of the gauge symmetry of the low energy M-theory compactifiation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide an explicit description of the entire network of phases for the low-energy gauge theory on the Coulomb branch, and in the geometric language this corresponds to the complete network of crepant resolutions for elliptically fibered fourfolds.

all elliptic Calabi–Yau fourfolds have a unique Weierstrass fibration, and the singularities of the Weierstraß model can be described in terms of decorated graphs, the box graphs, that encode the representation graph of matter fields.
the box graph description is a unification of the known fiber types for all Lie algebras, and furthermore, we predict a large number of new fiber types.

the geometry of elliptically fiberd Calabi-Yau varieties with section and their flop transitions are encoded in the representation theory of the matter multiplet.
